title: P72 (Papyrus Bodmer VIII): 1 Peter 1:1-2:2 (pages 1-6)
source: Papyrus Bodmer VIII (Vatican Library): photographs from DigiVatLib; Greek from the INTF NTVMR transcription of P72; English from the King James Version
description: 1 Peter 1:1-2:2 in P72, the 3rd/4th-century papyrus codex of 1-2 Peter and Jude: pages 1-6 of the papyrus, each with its photograph, the Greek transcription and the King James Version.
introduction:
P72 is a papyrus codex copied in Egypt in the 3rd or early 4th century. It holds the oldest known copies of 1 Peter, 2 Peter and Jude. The pages are numbered by the scribe. 1-2 Peter (papyrus pages 1-36) are Papyrus Bodmer VIII, given by Martin Bodmer to Pope Paul VI in 1969 and now in the Vatican Library; Jude (pages 62-68) is Papyrus Bodmer VII, still at the Fondation Martin Bodmer, Cologny (Geneva). Both belong to the Bodmer "Miscellaneous" or "Composite" codex, which also contains the Nativity of Mary, the apocryphal correspondence of Paul with the Corinthians, the 11th Ode of Solomon, Melito's sermon On the Pascha, a hymn fragment and other texts. 1-2 Peter seem to have formed a separate booklet before being bound with the rest.

Each section below is one papyrus page: the photograph, the NTVMR diplomatic transcription of that page line by line, and the King James Version of every verse on it. The scribe's spelling is irregular (ει for ι, ε for αι, and so on) and is kept as written.

This entry covers papyrus pages 1-6 (1 Peter 1:1-2:2). The photographs are from the Vatican Library (Pap. Bodmer VIII).
translator_notes: Greek: the NTVMR diplomatic transcription, line by line as on the papyrus. Square brackets enclose letters that are lost or illegible and were supplied by the transcribers; a dot under a letter marks it as uncertain; [...] marks a gap. Nomina sacra and numerals keep the scribe's overline. Spelling is the scribe's (no accents or breathings). Words broken at a line end stay broken as on the papyrus. Corrections are not shown: the text is the first hand.

English: the King James Version (1611), whole verses, for every verse that has text on the page. A verse that begins on one page and ends on the next is given in full on both. The KJV translates a later form of the Greek text, so its wording does not always match the papyrus; material differences (such as verses the papyrus does not have) are noted in the section.

translation.text: <sup>1:1</sup>Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, <sup>2</sup>Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification of the Spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace unto you, and peace, be multiplied. <sup>3</sup>Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, <sup>4</sup>To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you,
translation.scan_note: Vatican Library, Pap. Bodmer VIII, DigiVatLib image 2 (https://digi.vatlib.it/view/MSS_Pap.Bodmer.VIII/0002), the right-hand page of the opening, cropped at the fold. The typed label on the glass frame reads "p. 1 (A) 1 Petri 1, 1-4". Checked on the image: the page number A is at the head, then the title line πετρου επιστολη α (on the papyrus but not in the NTVMR transcription), then ‹πετρος αποστολος ι̅υ̅ χ̅ρ̅υ̅ εκλε›. The last full line is ‹[τον κ]α̣ι̣ αμαραντον τετηρημε› (1:4); the final transcribed line, ‹[νην εν ου]ρ̣α̣[νοις] ε̣ι̣ς̣ η̣μ̣α̣[ς]›, survives only as traces along the broken bottom edge.

translation.text: <sup>1:5</sup>Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time. <sup>6</sup>Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations: <sup>7</sup>That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ: <sup>8</sup>Whom having not seen, ye love; in whom, though now ye see him not, yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory: <sup>9</sup>Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls.
translation.scan_note: Vatican Library, Pap. Bodmer VIII, DigiVatLib image 1 (https://digi.vatlib.it/view/MSS_Pap.Bodmer.VIII/0001), the left-hand page of the opening, cropped at the fold. The typed label on the glass frame reads "I verso = p. 2 (B) 1 Petri 1, 5-9". 1:9 continues on the next page. Checked on the image: 17 lines in the transcription; the first legible line (line 1) reads ‹τος εν δ̅υ̅μ̅ι̅ φρουρουμενου δ̣›, the last legible line (line 16) ‹α̣ι δεδοξασμενη κομε̣›; both match the page.

translation.text: <sup>1:9</sup>Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls. <sup>10</sup>Of which salvation the prophets have enquired and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that should come unto you: <sup>11</sup>Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow. <sup>12</sup>Unto whom it was revealed, that not unto themselves, but unto us they did minister the things, which are now reported unto you by them that have preached the gospel unto you with the Holy Ghost sent down from heaven; which things the angels desire to look into. <sup>13</sup>Wherefore gird up the loins of your mind, be sober, and hope to the end for the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;

translation.text: <sup>1:13</sup>Wherefore gird up the loins of your mind, be sober, and hope to the end for the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ; <sup>14</sup>As obedient children, not fashioning yourselves according to the former lusts in your ignorance: <sup>15</sup>But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation; <sup>16</sup>Because it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy. <sup>17</sup>And if ye call on the Father, who without respect of persons judgeth according to every man’s work, pass the time of your sojourning here in fear: <sup>18</sup>Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers;

The typed label on the glass frame reads "II verso = p. 4 (Δ) 1 Petri 1, 13-18". 1:13 begins on the previous page; 1:18 continues on the next page. translation.text: <sup>1:18</sup>Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers; <sup>19</sup>But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot: <sup>20</sup>Who verily was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you, <sup>21</sup>Who by him do believe in God, that raised him up from the dead, and gave him glory; that your faith and hope might be in God. <sup>22</sup>Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently:

translation.text: <sup>1:22</sup>Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently: <sup>23</sup>Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever. <sup>24</sup>For all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass. The grass withereth, and the flower thereof falleth away: <sup>25</sup>But the word of the Lord endureth for ever. And this is the word which by the gospel is preached unto you. <sup>2:1</sup>Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings, <sup>2</sup>As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby:
